problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+1}{{x}^{3}(x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{C}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{D}{x+1},
$$

where $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are real constants, determine the value of $AB-CD.$

activity_context.topic_title: Expressing Rational Functions with Repeated Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+x+1}{{x}^{2}(x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{C}{x+1},
$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by ${x}^{2}(x+1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+x+1 & =Ax(x+1)+B(x+1)+C{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(0)^{2}+0+1 & =A(0)(0+1)+B(0+1)+C(0)^{2} \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-1$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-1)^{2}+(-1)+1 & =A(-1)(-1+1)+B(-1+1)+C(-1)^{2} \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=1$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}+1+1 & =A(1)(1+1)+(1)(1+1)+(3)(1)^{2} \\ 5 & =2A+2+3 \\ 5 & =2A+5 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Hence,

$$
A\cdot B\cdot C=0\cdot 1\cdot 3=0.
$$
